question.problem: If ${log}_{5}⁡(4-x)=2{log}_{5}⁡2,$ then what is the value of $x?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we use the power rule to simplify the right-hand side. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(4-x) & =2{log}_{5}⁡2 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(4-x) & ={log}_{5}⁡{2}^{2} \\ {log}_{5}⁡(4-x) & ={log}_{5}⁡4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(4-x) & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ 4-x & =4 \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=0$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(4-x) & ={log}_{5}⁡(4-0) \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(4) \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡({2}^{2}) \\  & =2{log}_{5}⁡2.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=0$ is a valid solution.
